The accepted laws (E2) cite fitted exponents of 2.90-3.02 from field studies with n of 117 to 2769 in flying fishes, which sit far outside this law's band. I did not fetch those sources, so this rests on the quoted E2 basis. A law that declares those populations false is wrong at the family scope. I have no measurement of a single named species that I saw directly. A b near 1 over a 0.257-0.340 m range is also implausible for somatic growth, which suggests measurement error (for example, mixed length kinds or sex/maturity mixing) in the 14 specimens.

The bound is the 95% CI of the fit to all 14 specimens, and the law is then 'tested' against that same fit: the witness b = 0.981 is the fitted slope. Nothing was held back, so it is circular by construction. A CI on a slope also does not bound the true slope of any other sample, and with r^2 = 0.601 and a ~8% length span the interval is mostly noise.

If accepted, it would turn RED any flying-fish design with a physically sensible cubic-ish mass exponent (2.9-3.02), which is what the large field studies in E2 report. It would also contradict E1/E2 in Lean for the whole family, so every design satisfying one law would fail the other. The optimizer would then be pushed toward an exponent of ~1, which is a fish with a mass that does not scale with volume.

C1_binds_something_real.gate_why: the candidate declares no shared_scope.atoms, so the studio has nothing to evaluate and the law binds no design today. The proposer says so itself (browser_check_absent: provable-but-not-checkable; it would need effective_population_size (Ne, individuals), neutral_mutation_rate_per_generation (mu), observed_heterozygosity (H)), and that supplied, it would reject: Rejects a design annotated with an effective population size and a neutral mutation rate whose stated neutral heterozygosity is outside (0,1) or is lower than that of a sibling design with a smaller Ne*mu.
C1_binds_something_real.referee_reason: The Lean witness is declared, but the candidate has shared_scope: null, so no atoms exist for the studio to evaluate and nonvacuity.mjs searched 0 assignments. The proponent exhibited a rejecting design as numbers (Ne=1000, mu=1e-5, H=0.9, against the 0.0385 the hypothesis gives). That design is an annotation the engine cannot carry, because sim-engine has no Ne, mu or H fields. This is the provable-but-not-checkable case, not a tautology fail. The fix is to declare the missing quantities.

C2_constants_sourced.gate_why: the statement carries no empirical constant (structural literals only), so there is nothing to source
C2_constants_sourced.referee_reason: The statement contains only structural literals. The factor 4 is part of the named hypothesis HetHyp, which is cited to Kimura & Crow 1964, and the evidence fetch found nothing to check. The critic's complaint that no equation number is given is minor and does not make the factor an empirical constant.

C3_scope_honest.referee_reason: scope.taxa is ['any'] and ranges is {}, so the structured scope names no ranges for Ne, mu or H. The conditions that actually limit the law (neutral locus, infinite alleles, constant Ne, equilibrium, diploid autosomal so that the factor is 4) appear only in the free-text basis. The proponent concedes it fails for haploid, X-linked and organellar loci. Nothing was observed in any organism (observations: []). The prose is candid, but the structured fields claim more than the basis supports. This is fixable by declaring the conditions, not by dropping the law.

C4_independent.referee_reason: No accepted law constrains equilibrium heterozygosity. kimura-fixation-probability (neutral fixation = initial frequency), favored-fixation-lower-bound and genotype-substitution-time concern substitution and fixation, and fisher-ftns concerns the rate of change of mean fitness. A design with correct 1/(2N) neutral fixation but H outside (0,1), or non-monotone in Ne*mu, passes all of those and fails this law. The critic's point that the law restates its own hypothesis is true but is not what C4 tests. HetHyp is a cited model result, not a definition by the meaning of its terms and not an accepted law. The range in (0,1) and the strict monotonicity are derived consequences of it. The content is thin but not null.

C5_consistent.referee_reason: propose.mjs built a joint witness with every overlapping accepted law, and the candidate matches no known open dispute.

The result is unclear, not pass, and so it blocks promotion.

C7_not_circular.referee_reason: No data were fitted. The statement is explicitly conditional ('Under the infinite-alleles equilibrium ... (a named hypothesis)'). It is a deduction from a stated model premise, not an observed extreme presented as an impossibility. The proponent's own bound_kind_why says it is model-internal, and the scope basis flags Lewontin's paradox against applying the hypothesis to real census sizes. The cost is that nothing empirical backs the law, which is a C6 and C3 matter, not circularity.

rulings.ruling: The law is a kernel-checked consequence of the Kimura-Crow infinite-alleles equilibrium: H lies strictly in (0,1) and rises strictly with Ne*mu. It is not a tautology and not a restatement of any accepted law, since none constrains heterozygosity. No hard gate failed, but two things block promotion. C1 and C6 are both unclear: the law declares no shared atoms, so the studio cannot evaluate it, and no wild-type organism was tested. C3 also fails, because 'any' taxa with empty ranges leaves the real limiting conditions only in prose. This is NEEDS-WORK and not REJECT because every defect is a missing mapping or a mis-stated scope, not a false claim or a record bound sold as an impossibility. It is not PROMOTE because an untestable law does not get to turn designs dashed.

proponent.strongest_sentence: Given a declared von Bertalanffy curve with Linf > 0 and K > 0, the Lean theorem proves that no age yields a length at or above Linf, that length rises strictly with age, and that same-K cohorts reach identical fractions of their own asymptote at identical ages since t0, so a design pairing a length with a curve that cannot produce it is malformed.
proponent.weakest_point: The theorem is algebra that follows from the hypothesis: the biology lives entirely in the assumption that the cohort follows VB, which rests on 12 secondary FishBase rows for 7 of 75 species and one validated row whose paper was not seen. The critic will say this is a tautology about a functional form, not a biological law, and that Linf is a fitted mean that real individuals exceed, so the browser check would flag real fish. In addition, growth_Linf_m is not an engine state field, so the check mostly returns cannot-evaluate.

rules_out.why_rejected: Under the fitted Hirundichthys affinis curve (Linf = 23.3 cm FL, K = 3.12/yr, t0 = 0.01 yr), length is strictly below Linf at every age, so a cohort claiming a length of 25 cm against a 23.3 cm asymptote is malformed: no age on that curve produces it. The same holds for any design whose length equals Linf exactly. The second clause also rejects a design that gives two cohorts the same K but different fractions of their own asymptote at equal age from their own t0.
rules_out.buildable_note: A designer can type SL = 0.25 m next to Linf = 0.233 m. Whether the animal can be 25 cm long is a separate matter: individuals routinely exceed a fitted Linf, because Linf is a mean asymptote, not a ceiling for individuals. The law rejects the pairing of that length with that curve, not the animal. The candidate's own browser_check note says this. Also, growth_Linf_m is not an engine state field today, so the check returns cannot-evaluate unless the design supplies it.

taxa: the 7 Exocoetidae species with a FishBase VB row, as compiled fits only
scope_supported.why: The strict bound is a theorem about a curve, so it holds for any VB cohort. The evidence that Exocoetidae follow VB is 12 secondary compilation rows over 7 of 75 species; only one is marked validated, and the paper itself was not seen. Nothing is established for the 68 species with no row or for embryos. Larva and juvenile coverage is thin, and the claimed 'larva' stage is supported mainly by the lab-rearing component of the one validated row. The honest scope is: conditional on the VB hypothesis, with that hypothesis supported for 7 species in the fitted locality and year.

independence.what_this_forbids_that_one_permits: E2 bounds the length-weight exponent b in [2.90, 3.02], so it constrains how mass scales with length for adults in a fitted size range. It says nothing about how length changes with age or about a ceiling. This law forbids a length at or above the fitted Linf, forbids non-monotone length-at-age, and forbids two same-K cohorts from differing in fractional attainment at equal age from t0. E2 permits all three. E5 (fin ratio) shares no quantity either.

critic.one_sentence: The Lean statement is a tautology of the von Bertalanffy formula that no organism can falsify, and the only operational content, SL < a fitted Linf, treats a mean curve parameter from a secondary compilation as a hard maximum length.

attacks.finding: The statement is a theorem about the functional form. Under the hypothesis Linf>0, K>0, Linf*(1-exp(-K(t-t0))) < Linf always holds, since exp>0. The conclusion is conditional on the hypothesis, and the hypothesis is part of the statement, so the statement cannot be falsified by any organism. The only content that could constrain a design is the hidden bridge (length < fitted Linf of the taxon), and that is not what the Lean theorem proves.
attacks.tried: Tried t -> infinity, t < t0 (length goes negative but still < Linf), very large K, very small K, and Linf vs Linf' with the same K. Every case satisfies all three conjuncts. Did not need any external data.
attacks.evidence: Algebraic: exp(x) > 0 for all real x, so 1 - exp(.) < 1. No fetch was needed.

attacks.finding: The statement has no constants, but the scope ranges and the default curve have numbers: Linf 23.3 cm, K 3.12/yr, t0 0.01 yr, and ranges Linf 13.5 to 30.5 and K 0.86 to 3.65. I did not search for or fetch a specific measurement, so I cannot name an animal and numbers. I have no measurement to report, so this is not a counterexample.

The scope ranges (Linf, K) are the min and max of the same 12 rows that make up the evidence, so nothing was held back. There is no independent test. Because the Lean statement is a theorem, no data test it either way. The 12 rows are also not independent: they are FishBase fits from several studies and may share underlying otolith or length-frequency data. n_independent is at most 7 species and probably fewer than 12 studies; I did not check.

As wired to the browser check, a design whose SL is at or above the Linf of its fitted taxon turns RED. A designer who wants a larger-than-average flying fish, which individuals within the wild population can be, would be blocked by a mean fitted parameter. Linf also has no engine field, so the check would be cannot-evaluate for most designs. I cannot name a specific lineage whose measurements exceed the bound, as I did not find a measurement.
